headline: Approved a $6M citywide vehicle bond and a $434,264 jail and arrest diversion grant, along with several smaller grants.
summary: The council heard reports on the June and August revenue and expenditure reports and the election warrant. It approved a $6M bond for city vehicles, grants for police, gaming harm, and parks, a Head Start resolution, a prior year bill, and a library donation.
decisions: Roll call on the informational FY 2026 June Revenue Vs. Expenditure Report recorded 12-0, with Malo Brown away. The minutes state no motion.
Roll call on the informational FY 2027 August Revenue Vs. Expenditure Report recorded 12-0, with Malo Brown away. The minutes state no motion.
Roll call on the Election Warrant recorded 12-0, with Malo Brown away. The minutes state no motion.
Approved the FY27 CMF- Gaming Harm Project grant of $75,000, with no match required, 12-0 with Malo Brown away.
Approved the Parks FY27 Greening the Gateway Cities Program Implementation Grant of $75,000, 12-0 with Malo Brown away.
Approved the CIT Training Reimbursement Grant, no match, of $100,000, 12-0 with Malo Brown away.
Approved the Jail / Arrest Diversion Program Grant, no match required, of $434,264.00, 12-0 with Malo Brown away.
Approved the Bill of Prior Year for the $48 bill from HR/LR, 12-0 with Malo Brown away.
Approved the $100 donation from Barbara Garvey to the Indian Orchard Branch Library, 12-0 with Malo Brown away.
Approved the $6M bond authorization for city wide vehicles in FY27, 13-0.
Approved the Head Start & Early Head Start Resolution, 13-0.

City Council  
     
Regular Meeting 
 
~Final~ 
   
 
36 Court Street  
Springfield, MA 01103   
http://www.springfieldcityhall.com 
 
Gladys Oyola-Lopez 
 
October 5, 2026 6:30 PM City Hall - Room 200 
 
 
 
Roll Call 
COUNCILORS SANTANIELLO AND PEREZ WERE REMOTE FOR THIS MEETING. 
COUNCILOR FENTON ARRIVED LATE AT 6:42PM, COUNCILOR BROWN ARRIVED 
AT 7:22PM. 
Moment Of Silence - Pledge Of Allegiance 
 
Reports Of Committee 
COUNCILOR WALSH REPORTED ON THE ELDER AFFAIRS MEETING THAT WAS 
HELD LAST WEEK TOPIC WAS SENIOR SCAMS.  SPD ADVISED TO NOT PICK UP 
THE PHONE. 
COUNCILOR GOVAN REPORTED ON THE FINANCE COMMITTEE MEETING FROM 
9/28, THE SPRINGFIELD PARKING AUTHORITY WAS THE TOPIC.  THEY ALSO MET 
TODAY BEFORE THIS MEETING TO DISCUSS FINANCE ITEMS ON THE AGENDA. 
COUNCILOR MARTIN STATED THAT PUBLIC SAFETY AND HEALTH AND HUMAN 
SERVICES HELD A JOINT MEETING AND THE TOPIC WAS KRATOM AND HOW TO 
CONFISCATE LEGALLY. 
COUNCILOR DAVILA REPORTED ON THE ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE 
MEETING FROM 9/24. 
 
Informational 
 1. FY 2026 June Revenue Vs. Expenditure Report  
COMPTROLLER PATRICK BURNS SPOKE ON THE REPORT. 
COUNCILOR SANTANIELLO ASKED SPECIFICS IN THE FINAL REPORT. 
COUNCILOR FENTON STATED THE SPECIAL COMMITTEE ON TARGETED TAX 
RELIEF HAS BEEN MEETING REGULARLY.  APPLICATIONS WILL BE GETTING 
DISTRIBUTED NEXT WEEK.
COUNCILOR CLICK BRUCE WOULD LIKE THE BODY TO SEE WHERE THE 
MARIJUANA FUNDS CAN BE USED. 
 
AYES Brian Santaniello, Gerry Martin, Maria Perez, Zaida Govan, Kateri 
Walsh, Justin Hurst, Victor Davila, Michael Fenton, Jose Delgado, 
Lavar Click-Bruce, Melvin Edwards, Tracye Whitfield 
NAYS None

COLLECTION OF MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE TAXES, ALONG WITH PENALTIES.
